comment: No source is published. The panel is a drawing with no lettering on any control, so every name used here is the maker's own from the tooltips. The modulation oscillator is a parabolic shape built in line, running at fifteen times the modulation-rate knob, and its output is multiplied by 6000 and by the modulation-depth knob before being added to the clock rate. A Mersenne twister adds a noise floor of about a thousandth either way to the output, which is what gives the module its hiss. The feedback path is clamped to plus and minus 0.3 and then lowpassed, so the module self-oscillates rather than running away. The switch parameter is a latch, and the flag it produces selects between two branches inside the delay input stage; what the two branches do differently was not settled, so the line says only that.
